title: Match and destructure
summary: match takes data apart by shape - and the compiler insists you handle every shape.
lecture: A match arm is a shape with holes: `Event::Click(x, y)` both tests the variant AND binds its fields in one motion. No casts, no getters - the pattern is the access.

Exhaustiveness is the superpower: the compiler rejects a match that misses a variant. Add a variant next month and every match that needs updating becomes a compile error - a to-do list you can't ignore.
That's why a wildcard `_` arm deserves suspicion: it compiles today and silently absorbs the variants of tomorrow. Name the variants you handle; reserve `_` for genuinely don't-care cases.
For a single interesting case, `if let Some(v) = maybe { … }` says it smaller than a match with an empty arm.

example.caption: Test the shape, bind the parts, forget nothing.
